title: Token Bucket Implementation
description: Implement a production-grade token bucket rate limiter in Redis with atomic Lua scripts and proper response headers.

data.text: A token bucket implementation must be atomic under concurrent access. Using Redis Lua scripts ensures the refill, decrement, and decision happen in a single operation. This prevents race conditions where two simultaneous requests see the same token balance.
Store one hash per rate limit key. The hash tracks the bucket state. TTL is set to the bucket capacity divided by refill rate to keep storage bounded.

data.title: Redis Lua script for atomic token bucket
data.content: The script runs atomically on Redis. No race conditions are possible.
data.code:
-- KEYS[1] = rate limit key (e.g., rate:user:123)
-- ARGV[1] = capacity (e.g., 100)
-- ARGV[2] = refill rate per second (e.g., 10)
-- ARGV[3] = now in milliseconds

local key = KEYS[1]
local capacity = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local refill_rate = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local now = tonumber(ARGV[3])

local bucket = redis.call('HMGET', key, 'tokens', 'last_refill')
local tokens = tonumber(bucket[1]) or capacity
local last_refill = tonumber(bucket[2]) or now

-- Calculate elapsed time and refill
local elapsed = math.max(0, now - last_refill) / 1000
local tokens_to_add = elapsed * refill_rate
tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + tokens_to_add)

-- Try to consume 1 token
local allowed = 0
local remaining = 0
local retry_after = 0

if tokens >= 1 then
    tokens = tokens - 1
    allowed = 1
    remaining = tokens
else
    retry_after = math.ceil((1 - tokens) / refill_rate)
end

-- Update state
redis.call('HMSET', key, 'tokens', tokens, 'last_refill', now)
redis.call('EXPIRE', key, math.ceil(capacity / refill_rate))

return { allowed, remaining, retry_after }

data.title: Rate limiter middleware using Redis and Lua
data.content: Apply rate limiting per API key or user ID with standard rate limit headers.

data.text: Token bucket naturally supports bursts because the bucket can accumulate tokens during idle periods. A client that is idle for 10 seconds with a rate of 10/s builds up 100 tokens, allowing a burst of 100 requests instantly.

data.title: Per-endpoint limits
data.text: Use different rate limit keys per endpoint tier: /api/search might be 10 req/min, while /api/health is unlimited. Combine per-user and per-endpoint dimensions in the Redis key: rate:user:123:search.

items.question: Do I need Lua scripts if I use Redis single-threaded mode?
items.answer: Yes. Even single-threaded Redis can interleave commands from different clients. Without a Lua script, two clients could read the same token balance, both see tokens > 0, and both consume. The Lua script makes the read-modify-write atomic.

items.question: What if Redis is down?
items.answer: Fail open (allow requests) if availability is critical, or fail closed (reject all requests) if protecting downstream is critical. Most APIs fail open during Redis outages to avoid total service unavailability.

items.question: How do I reset a user's rate limit?
items.answer: Delete the Redis key: DEL rate:user:123. The next request will create a fresh bucket with full capacity. Use this for support resets.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Token bucket state lives in a Redis hash with two numeric fields.
Lua scripts make refill and decrement atomic under concurrency.
Return standard rate limit headers so clients can self-regulate.
Fail open on Redis outages unless protecting downstream is critical.
data.takeaway: A token bucket in Redis is one Lua script away from production. The script is the entire concurrency story — get it right and your rate limiter is correct under any load pattern.
